answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can implement transitive trust graphs that leave hollow identity clusters isolated. Rejecting ivory tower assumptions about digital honesty, agents only extend credit along paths validated by reputable seed nodes, such as enterprise juniper routers. An attacker incurs the verifiable, scarce cost of acquiring genuine trust edges for every identity. However, this mechanism restricts onboarding for unvetted newcomers and entrenches legacy nodes.
